builtFrom: fetch-and-verify fleet (5 domain researchers) + 1 adversarial verifier, 2026-08-20

READ_THIS_FIRST.whatWentRight: ZERO FABRICATED SOURCES. The verifier hunted specifically for invented papers, re-fetched 19 sources, and every one hosts the work claimed - including two whose identifiers looked wrong for their publication year and checked out. Sources are real and correctly identified.
READ_THIS_FIRST.theRealFailureMode: EPISTEMIC DRIFT, and it is quieter than fabrication. Five recorded quotes did not survive re-fetch, and EVERY ONE DRIFTED IN THE SAME DIRECTION: toward more certainty. The clearest: a source's 'This suggests that' was recorded as 'We conclude that'. A conclusion is not a suggestion. These rows are quarantined, not deleted.
READ_THIS_FIRST.theTrapForDownstreamReaders: APPARENT CORROBORATION THAT IS ONE UNREAD PAPER. Several numbers look supported by four independent sources; the verifier traced every path back to a single paywalled paper that nobody in this fleet read. See citationChainWarnings on the affected rows.
READ_THIS_FIRST.quoteFidelityCaveat: Rows marked VIA_SUMMARISING_FETCH_LAYER carry quotes as returned by a fetch layer that summarises pages - they are quotes-as-returned, not byte-for-byte copies. Rows marked RAW_BYTE_EXACT_SUBSTRING_MATCH were checked against raw downloaded bytes by exact substring match; those are the strongest rows in the inventory. Anyone republishing should re-verify against the source text.
READ_THIS_FIRST.auditCoverage: PARTIAL, AND THE CAUSE WAS OURS. The verifier was handed a TRUNCATED copy of the inventory (the orchestration sliced its input at 180,000 characters), so it audited roughly three and a half of five domains and correctly reported two domains 'missing with no failure note'. That was our defect, not the researchers'. All five domains did arrive; comparators and frames-and-fringe are UNAUDITED and their rows carry verification NOT_SPOT_CHECKED.
READ_THIS_FIRST.languageContract: The verifier found NO use of 'fact' or 'proven' about any claim, and source hedging preserved in the great majority of rows. The eight exceptions it did find are recorded in languageViolations and their rows are quarantined or flagged.
READ_THIS_FIRST.quarantineIsBroaderThanRefetchFailure: Quarantine (18 rows) is BROADER than quote-reproduction failure (5 rows). The verifier also quarantined rows that assert past their source hedging, and rows whose independence claim failed. Every quarantined row now carries quarantineCauses naming what was actually recorded FOR THAT ROW; where the verifier named no per-row reason we say so rather than inventing one.
READ_THIS_FIRST.deliveryVsResearchFailure: One row (SC-12) was previously labelled QUOTE_NOT_REPRODUCED_ON_REFETCH. That was OUR mislabel: the verifier recorded URL_DEAD and explained it was a DELIVERY failure caused by our own 180,000-character truncation of its input. It now reads DELIVERY_TRUNCATED_BY_ORCHESTRATION. A tooling defect must never be recorded against the work it examined.

publishedPaperDefect.source: Mora et al. (2009), PLoS Computational Biology
publishedPaperDefect.finding: The paper states '~1.7 degrees, which corresponds to 26 steps per rotation'. 1.7 does not give 26; 13.7 does. The verifier re-fetched and confirmed the sentence is real.
publishedPaperDefect.ruling: The arithmetic defect is IN THE PUBLISHED PAPER, not in our transcription. Recorded, not corrected by us.

spotChecks.detail: Re-fetched cambridge.org/core Sowa & Berry 2008. Full text IS accessible (not paywalled as I expected). Exact string present: "The estimated flux was around 1200 H+ ions per revolution per motor over a speed range of ~20-60 Hz". The row's own caveat stands: this is the REVIEW's restatement; the primary (Meister 1987) was never read.

Same page. Exact string present: "With a typical IMF of around -150 mV, the free energy of a single ion transit is ~6 kBT." Also confirmed "The most probable step size of 13.7 degrees corresponds to 26 steps per revolution (360/13.7=26.3)."

Same page. Exact string present: "The stoichiometry of stator complexes deduced from targeted disulphide cross-linking studies and chromatography appears to be A4B2". The deliberate retention of a falsified claim is good practice and is correctly labelled.

Re-fetched PLoS Comput Biol 1000540. BOTH strings present verbatim: "~10 protons passing through the membrane per MotA/B unit per rotation" AND "The steps have average size ~1.7 degrees, which corresponds to 26 steps per rotation, exactly the number of copies of FliG around the rotor." The 1.7-vs-26 arithmetic inconsistency is IN THE PUBLISHED SOURCE, not a transcription artefact. The researcher hedged this as possibly fetch-layer damage; it is not. Correct the confidenceNote to say the defect is the paper's.

Re-fetched PMC7610383. Exact string present: "3D reconstructions of these complexes yielded volumes that could only be interpreted as MotA5B2 assemblies". BUT the confidenceNote contains a verifiable factual error - see languageViolations and corroborations. IF-02 ("TMH3 and TMH4 line the central pore") and IF-19 ("plug helices are not the sole block to ion permeation") also verified on the same fetch.

Re-fetched PMC11725901 TWICE. The recorded verbatimQuote "Cavity-I is a size filter for sodium ions." does NOT exist as a sentence. It exists as a RESULTS subsection HEADING in title case: "Cavity-I Is a Size Filter for Sodium Ions" (no terminal period). The quoteLocator says "Discussion - ion selectivity" and that is WRONG. The nearest actual Discussion sentence is materially weaker: "Thus, Cavity-I is not a simple ion path but contributes to the selection of sodium ions as a size filter." Substance survives; the citation does not. Fix casing, punctuation, locator, and prefer the weaker prose sentence.

The only 36-degree sentence my fetch surfaced is a figure-legend sentence about accessible rotation angles rotating by 36 degrees when protonated binding sites are swapped. The claim may still be in the paper elsewhere, but I could not reproduce this string. IF-09 is the premise IF-10 is derived from, so this is load-bearing.

Same page. Exact string present: "Ten ions per revolution of the MotA pentamer then correspond to 10 x 34/5 = 68 ions per MotAB stator unit per revolution of the flagellar motor." Correctly labelled DERIVED. IF-08 ("narrow H+ channels") also verified. Re-fetched the Santiveri bioRxiv preprint. Recorded quote opens "We conclude that CjMotB chain 1 D22...". The source sentence my fetch returned opens "This suggests that CjMotB chain 1 D22, but not CjMotB chain 2 D22, would be protonatable and/or able to interact with hydronium." The predicate matches; the epistemic verb does NOT. "We conclude" is materially stronger than "This suggests". This is exactly the class of drift the anti-fabrication protocol exists to catch.

STRUCTURAL, AND THE LARGEST: the brief says five researchers. THREE domains arrived. Two are absent with no failure note. I am not going to speculate about what they contained.
corroborations: MotA5B2 5:2 STOICHIOMETRY - IF-01 and MS-27 are THE SAME PAPER in two versions (Deme et al., Nature Microbiology author manuscript PMC7610383 vs bioRxiv 2020.05.12.089201) carrying THE SAME SENTENCE. This is a duplicate presented across two domains, NOT independent triangulation. Same for IF-19 and MS-28, which quote the identical 'plug helices are not the sole block' sentence.

STATOR PLUG BLOCKS ION FLOW - genuinely triangulated four ways across two domains: IF-17 (Homma & Kojima 2022), IF-18 (Santiveri preprint), IF-20 (Nakamura & Minamino 2019), IF-24 (Hu et al. 2023), MS-28 (Deme preprint). The deletion phenotype is agreed by every source; only the sufficiency of the plug is contested.

CONSERVED MotB ASPARTATE AS PROTON ACCEPTOR - IF-03 (Zhou 1998, primary genetics, E. coli Asp32), IF-04 (Nakamura & Minamino review, Salmonella Asp33), MS-27 (Deme, MotB D32 in a ring of MotA T209). Three sources, two independent of each other in authorship. Strongest-supported residue-level claim in the inventory.

LOAD-DEPENDENT STATOR RECRUITMENT - MS-01 (Lele/Berg, speed steps) and MS-04 (Tipping/Berry/Armitage, fluorescence intensity). Different laboratories, different readouts, same direction. Genuine triangulation and the researcher identified it correctly.
CATCH BOND / TORQUE-STABILISED STATOR - MS-07, MS-08 (Nord/Pedaci/Berry) and MS-17, MS-19, MS-20 (Wadhwa/Tu/Berg). Two laboratories, two methods. Genuine.

Na+ SITE-2 THREONINES T158/T185/T186 - IF-22/IF-23 (Hu et al., cryo-EM coordination) and IF-25 (Onoue et al., mutational genetics). Structure and genetics converge from different first authors. The researcher called this genuine triangulation and I agree.

MOTOR HILL COEFFICIENT ~10 - SC-01 (Sourjik & Berg's REFIT of Cluzel's data), SC-08 (Antani et al. ASSUMING h=10 'based on previous studies'), plus Yuan 2012 and Ma 2012 named in the searchLog. THIS IS NOT TRIANGULATION. Every path traces to Cluzel, Surette & Leibler (2000), Science, which is closed-access (Unpaywall: oa_status 'closed', no OA location, no PMC deposit) and was NEVER READ by anyone. Four sources agreeing because they all cite one unread paper is a single source wearing four coats. Same for K_D = 3.1 microM.

CROSS-DOMAIN OVERLAP: torque-gated stator occupancy appears as MS-01/MS-04/MS-07/MS-17 (mechanosensing) and SC-07/SC-09 (switch-chemotaxis, Antani et al. 2021). Note Antani, Gupta, Lee, Rhee, Manson & Lele shares a senior author with MS-01 (Lele) and MS-25/MS-26 (Chawla, Ford & Lele). These are NOT independent groups.

CONTESTED SOURCE HANDLED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS BY TWO RESEARCHERS: Biquet-Bisquert et al. 2021 (Front Microbiol 12:659464). The ion-flux researcher INCLUDED it as IF-34 and IF-35. The mechanosensing researcher fetched the same paper, could not re-verify its quotes against raw bytes, and EXCLUDED IT ENTIRELY. Same source, opposite calls, in one inventory. IF-34/IF-35 therefore rest on a method a peer explicitly judged insufficient.
contradictions: STATOR STOICHIOMETRY 4:2 vs 5:2. Sowa & Berry (2008) QRB 41(2): 'appears to be A4B2' (IF-32, VERIFIED by me). Deme et al. (2020) Nat Microbiol 5:1553: 'could only be interpreted as MotA5B2 assemblies' (IF-01/MS-27, VERIFIED by me). Not resolved. Every ions-per-revolution figure depends on which is used.

IONS PER STATOR UNIT PER REVOLUTION ~10 vs 68, a factor of seven. Mora et al. (2009) PLoS Comput Biol 5:e1000540 (IF-11, VERIFIED) vs Rieu et al. (2022) Front Microbiol 13:948383 (IF-10, VERIFIED). Both start from 'ten ions per revolution' but of different objects - per motor rotation vs per MotA pentamer rotation, geared 34/5.

PROTONS PER MOTOR REVOLUTION ~1200 vs everything else. Sowa & Berry (2008) (IF-12, VERIFIED) cannot be squared with IF-11 (~110) or IF-10 (~750). Species differs (Streptococcus vs E. coli/Salmonella) and the review hedges the figure itself.

IS THE PLUG THE GATE? Homma & Kojima (2022) Front Microbiol 13:869187 and Nakamura & Minamino (2019) Biomolecules 9:279 say the plug closes the channel (IF-17, IF-20). Deme et al. (2020) say 'the plug helices are not the sole block to ion permeation since there are no detectable channels across the cytoplasmic membrane compartment' (IF-19, VERIFIED).

DOES REMOVING THE PLUG OPEN THE PERIPLASMIC ENTRY? Santiveri et al. (2020 preprint, C. jejuni MotAB): access pathway exists unplugged, not plugged (IF-05, VERIFIED). Nishikino et al. (2025) PNAS 122:e2415713122 (marine Vibrio PomAB): 'The periplasmic side of the tunnel is closed' even after plug removal (IF-26, VERIFIED as a sentence though not as the recorded quote). Different species, different coupling ion, opposite conclusions.

SELECTIVITY FILTER LOCATION IN THE SAME PROTEIN. Hu et al. (2023) Nat Commun 14:4411 place it at three threonines with 'H+ is too small to fill this cavity' (IF-23, VERIFIED). Nishikino et al. (2025) place it in periplasmic Cavity-I, ~6 Angstrom hydrophobic, with those same threonines instead making CYTOPLASMIC Cavity-II hydrophilic (IF-26, VERIFIED). Both Vibrio PomAB, both cryo-EM, both a size filter, different locations.

IS MOTOR SPEED LINEAR IN PMF? Biquet-Bisquert et al. (2021) Front Microbiol 12:659464 report the consensus for linearity AND, in the same section, 'a decrease of pH_ext from 7 to 5 leads to a total decrease in PMF of only ~10 mV, yet causes a strong decline in motor speed' (IF-35). NOT SPOT-CHECKED BY ME - and see the corroborations note: a peer researcher excluded this source for unverifiable quotes.

PMF / MEMBRANE POTENTIAL MAGNITUDE, four numbers, not averaged. -165 mV measured (Kashket 1985, IF-29, VERIFIED). -160 mV measured (Krasnopeeva et al. 2019 Biophys J 116:2390, IF-30). '~-150 mV' typical (Sowa & Berry 2008, IF-31, VERIFIED). '120 mV' assumed and unsigned (Bai et al. 2009 Biophys J 96:3154, IF-37, VERIFIED). Terradot preprint uses -140 mV with a -90 mV dpH component (IF-36).

CIRCULARITY, not a contradiction but worse: IF-30 (Krasnopeeva) and IF-36 (Terradot) both MEASURE PMF USING MOTOR SPEED, assuming the speed-PMF linearity that IF-35 strains. Kashket (IF-29) is the only non-circular anchor and it is abstract-only. The foundational linearity primary, Gabel & Berg (2003) PNAS 100:8748, returned HTTP 403 and was never read by anyone.

ROTATION vs TORQUE AS THE SENSED VARIABLE - the sharpest in the inventory. Wadhwa, Tu & Berg (2021) PNAS 118:e2024608118: 'torque is the main parameter governing load-dependent stator remodeling', with no data collapse against speed (MS-17/MS-18, VERIFIED). Ito, Nakamura & Toyabe (2021) Nat Commun 12:3218: 'the binding is regulated not by the load on the previously bound stator units even at small N but by the rotation rate' (MS-22, VERIFIED). Same year, same symmetry experiment, opposite conclusions. Organism differs (E. coli vs Salmonella); NEITHER source offers that as the reconciliation. The one paper that attempts reconciliation (Biomolecules 15(3):355) returned HTTP 403 to the researcher.

STALL - MOST STATORS OR FEWEST? Tipping et al. (2013) mBio 4:e00551-13: 'motor stall... induced the largest number of bound stators that we observed' and rotation not required (MS-05/MS-06). Ito et al. (2021): 'The stator binding is slow at the stalled state' (MS-21, VERIFIED). Nord et al. (2017) PNAS 114:12952 sits between them (MS-11).

STATOR OCCUPANCY AT ZERO LOAD - 1-2 UNITS OR ZERO? Lele, Hosu & Berg (2013) PNAS 110:11839: 'one or sometimes two stator elements drive a motor near zero load' (MS-02). Wadhwa, Phillips & Berg (2019) PNAS 116:11764: 'varied from ~10 near stall to 0 at zero load' (MS-15, VERIFIED). Both E. coli, both Berg lab, six years apart.

DOES SPEED AFFECT THE ON RATE? Wadhwa/Phillips/Berg 2019 abstract: 'speed affects the binding rate and torque affects the free energy of bound stator units' (MS-13, VERIFIED against the complete abstract). Wadhwa/Tu/Berg 2021 Fig. 4: k+ = 0.0016 s-1 fitted TORQUE-INDEPENDENT (MS-19, VERIFIED). Same senior author, two years apart.

WHERE IS THE FORCE-GATED BOND? Nord et al. (2017) at the cell wall: the PG/MotB-PGB interface (MS-09). Chawla, Ford & Lele (2017) Sci Rep 7:5565 at the rotor: 'torque... modulates the accessibility of cryptic binding sites' (MS-26). Both hypotheses, both hedged.

THE CATCH BOND IS KINETICALLY INFERRED AND STRUCTURALLY UNOBSERVED. Nord et al.: 'While our data indicate a catch-bond mechanism, they cannot discriminate any structural detail' (MS-10). Deme et al. could not resolve the very domain: 'the PGB-domain of MotB has no fixed location with respect to the core complex' (MS-29). No source read provides a structural observation of the proposed force-bearing interface.

ON-RATES DIFFER BY ~3 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE. Wadhwa/Tu/Berg k+ = 0.0016 s-1 (MS-19, VERIFIED) vs Ito et al. b = 1.3 +/- 0.1 s-1 and k = 0.080 s-1 (MS-24, VERIFIED). Different models, organisms, definitions; no conversion established.

ULTRASENSITIVITY IS NOT IN THE BINDING STEP. Sourjik & Berg (2002) PNAS 99:12669 report motor Hill 10.3 against FliM-occupancy Hill 1.7 +/- 0.3 in the SAME paper (SC-01, SC-02, both VERIFIED). Two Hill coefficients for the binding data appear in the same section (1.7 +/- 0.3 and 1.8 +/- 0.3); the researcher recorded both rather than choosing, which is correct.

FliM COUNT: FIXED OR VARIABLE? Sarkar, Paul & Blair (2010) give 'about 25 FliG, 35 FliM, and 140 FliN' with no rotational condition stated (SC-10, VERIFIED). The truncated portion of the same inventory references FliM ring remodelling with a state-dependent count (Lele 2012, Yuan 2012, Hosu & Berg 2018) that DISAGREES on both driver and CCW count - but those rows were never delivered, so the contradiction is asserted in a confidenceNote with no evidence behind it.

APPARENT CONTRADICTION THAT IS NOT ONE: the conserved aspartate is Asp32 (E. coli), Asp33 (Salmonella), D22 (C. jejuni), D24 (Vibrio PomB). Nakamura & Minamino state the first correspondence explicitly. NO source read this session states the C. jejuni or Vibrio alignments, so those two are UNVERIFIED and must not be merged.
languageViolations: IF-01 confidenceNote: 'Triangulated in this session by two independent groups: Santiveri et al. and Hu et al.' THIS IS FALSE AND I CAN PROVE IT FROM A PAGE I FETCHED. The Hu et al. (2023) author list printed at PMC10374538 includes Monica Santiveri, Aritz Roa-Eguiara, Marc Erhardt and Nicholas M. I. Rieu et al. 2022 (IF-08/IF-09/IF-10) ALSO carries Taylor as an author; the researcher caught that dependency for Rieu and missed it for Hu.

IF-26 signalName: 'Cavity-I is a size filter for sodium ions' presented as a flat declarative verbatim sentence. The source's Discussion prose is weaker - 'contributes to the selection of sodium ions as a size filter' - and the same paper says selectivity involves 'a balance of multiple factors'. The confidenceNote hedges correctly; the signalName and verbatimQuote do not.
IF-07: 'We conclude that' substituted for the source's 'This suggests that'. A conclusion is not a suggestion. This is the single clearest instance of epistemic upgrade in the inventory.

IF-03 signalName: 'MotB Asp32 IS the proton-binding site (E. coli)'. The source says 'We propose that'. The confidenceNote flags the hedge; the name asserts past it. Under the operator's contract this should read 'proposed proton-binding site' or 'standing durable measure with observed genetic evidence'.

IF-13 signalName appends '(tight coupling)' as a parenthetical settled label. The abstract says the finding 'supports the hypothesis that the movement of protons through the motor is tightly coupled' - support for a hypothesis, not an established coupling. Minor but it is the load-bearing assumption of the whole ion-flux domain.
SC-11 signalName states a two-stage capture mechanism as a described process. The authors write 'Accordingly, we propose that...'. The confidenceNote catches it; the name does not.

IF-37 mechanismStated presents 'we enforce the tight coupling assumption by high potential barriers' as source wording. My re-fetch returned ABSENT for that string. Presenting an unverified string as an author quote inside the field that carries the row's epistemic warning is the worst place to have an unverified quote.

GENERAL, AND IN THE INVENTORY'S FAVOUR: I found NO instance of the word 'fact' or 'proven' used of a claim. Source hedges - 'appears to', 'is proposed to', 'likely', 'may', 'suggesting', 'we propose' - are preserved verbatim in the great majority of rows. Adverse and null results (IF-19, IF-35, MS-10, MS-25, MS-29) are recorded as first-class signals rather than buried. Superseded claims are retained deliberately (IF-32). On the operator's language contract, this inventory is in substantially better shape than its citation hygiene.
audit.verdict:
ADVERSE RESULT FIRST: this inventory is INCOMPLETE AS DELIVERED, and that is a bigger problem than anything I found inside it. The brief says five researchers. Three domains arrived. The third — switch-chemotaxis — terminates mid-string inside SC-12, and its contradictions and couldNotVerify arrays are gone entirely. Its own searchLog claims 15 documents fetched and its surviving rows forward-reference SC-13, SC-17 and SC-18, which do not exist in the data I was given. Two whole domains are missing with no failure note. Do not publish this as a complete inventory of five.

SECOND ADVERSE RESULT: I found ZERO fabricated sources. Every one of the 19 URLs I re-fetched hosts the work claimed, including the two I picked specifically because their PMC identifiers looked wrong for their publication years — PMC12978880 really is Huang, Wahlbeck Lu-Diaz, Thompson & Chen (2026) in Biophysical Journal, and PMC11107704 really is Salah Ud-Din & Roujeinikova (2017) in CMLS. I went looking for invented papers and there are none. What I found instead is EPISTEMIC DRIFT: four quotes that do not survive re-fetch, and in every single case the drift runs in the direction of MORE CERTAINTY. IF-07 turns the source's "This suggests that" into "We conclude that". IF-26 turns a Results heading into a Discussion sentence and files it under a wrong locator. IF-09, the premise from which IF-10's 68-ions figure is derived, I could not reproduce at all. That is the failure mode to worry about here, and it is quieter than fabrication.

THIRD: IF-01 asserts its 5:2 stoichiometry is "triangulated by two independent groups". It is not, and I can prove it from a page I fetched — the Hu et al. author list at PMC10374538 contains Santiveri, Roa-Eguiara, Erhardt and Taylor, the same people as Santiveri et al. 2020. One laboratory wearing two coats. Rieu et al. is the same lab again. The researcher caught this dependency for Rieu and missed it for Hu.

FOURTH, and this is the one that will bite a downstream model: the motor Hill coefficient of ~10 and the K_D of 3.1 μM appear to be corroborated by four sources. They are not. Every path traces to Cluzel, Surette & Leibler (2000) in Science, which Unpaywall reports as closed with no open location and no PMC deposit, and which NOBODY read. Four papers agreeing because they all cite one unread paper is a single source, not a triangulation. The same shape recurs for Meister 1987 (~1200 H+/rev, abstract only, primary 403) and Gabel & Berg 2003 (speed-proportional-to-PMF, never read by anyone, and the foundation two other rows silently assume).

ON THE ARITHMETIC ODDITY THE FIRST RESEARCHER FLAGGED: Mora et al.'s "~1.7°, which corresponds to 26 steps per rotation" is REAL. I fetched it. 1.7 does not give 26; 13.7 does. The defect is in the published paper, not in the fetch layer. The researcher hedged that it might be transcription damage — correct the note, the paper says it.

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOLID: 20 of 24 spot-checked quote-strings verified exactly, including several tells that only real reading produces — the middle-dot decimal in Wadhwa's "0⋅047", the absurd "± 0.0" uncertainties in Antani's fitted K_D, and the confirmed ABSENCE of "F186" from Rieu, which one researcher had already reported as an honest negative. The mechanosensing researcher's method is the strongest in the inventory: they distrusted WebFetch's summarizing layer, re-downloaded raw bytes via PowerShell, exact-substring-matched all 25 candidate quotes, caught a dropped "Hence," and reported catching it. That researcher's rows should carry more weight than mine — my verification ran through the SAME summarizing layer they rejected, so my QUOTE_VERIFIED is a second opinion from a second instrument of the same class, not byte-level proof. Where I disagree with them, defer to the command they ran, not to me.

GOVERNANCE FINDING: two researchers handled the SAME source oppositely. Biquet-Bisquert et al. 2021 was included by the ion-flux researcher as IF-34 and IF-35 and EXCLUDED ENTIRELY by the mechanosensing researcher, who fetched it, could not re-verify its quotes against raw bytes, and said so. IF-35 is the inventory's principal adverse row against speed-PMF linearity, and it rests on a method a peer judged insufficient. That must be resolved before either row is used.

FRACTION GENUINELY VERIFIABLE: of the 82 signals delivered, I directly re-verified 24 quote-strings across 19 sources; 20 held exactly, 4 did not. Extrapolating conservatively, roughly 80–85% of the delivered rows are quote-accurate to the source, and essentially 100% cite real, correctly-identified works. But quote-accuracy is not the binding constraint. About a quarter of the rows are derived, assumed, modelled, simulated, secondhand, abstract-only, or preprint-only — and the inventory says so, row by row, which is why it is trustworthy at all. The honest headline is: SOURCES REAL, QUOTES MOSTLY EXACT, INDEPENDENCE OVERSTATED IN AT LEAST TWO PLACES, FOUR QUOTES DRIFTED TOWARD CERTAINTY, TWO DOMAINS MISSING.

QUARANTINE (keep, mark unverified, do not show as standing): the four drifted quotes IF-06, IF-07, IF-09, IF-26 and SC-05; IF-37's unverified mechanismStated string; the entire truncated SC-12 and everything after it; IF-34 and IF-35 pending the peer-disputed source; SC-01, SC-08, MS-02, MS-31, MS-32 and IF-12 as secondhand quantities whose primaries no one read; IF-15, IF-16 and IF-36 as abstract-only or preprint-only rows whose free full texts existed and were not taken.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE INVENTORY OWES ITSELF, both provable from pages I fetched: IF-03 and IF-29 each state that no DOI is printed on the fetched page. Both DOIs ARE printed — 10.1128/jb.180.10.2729-2735.1998 and 10.1128/jb.163.2.423-429.1985. IF-22/IF-24/IF-25 state the Hu et al. author list was not returned; all eleven authors are on the page. The refusal to guess was right every time. The claim about what the page contained was wrong every time — a summarizer's silence was recorded as an observed absence. That is this estate's own "silence is not a value" defect, committed inside an anti-fabrication protocol written to prevent exactly it.

A verifier that finds nothing did not look. I looked, and what I found is not invention — it is over-confidence in the seams: in what a source concluded versus suggested, in whether two papers are two groups, and in whether a number four papers repeat was ever measured by any of them.

TRANSCRIPTION-RISK CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY ROW: WebFetch renders each page through a summarising model, so each "verbatim" string below is a quote as that layer returned it from the fetched page, not a byte-for-byte copy I made myself from raw HTML. Where a returned quote contained ellipses (Hu et al. 2023 translocation-pathway sentence) I trimmed to the contiguous fragment and flagged it. One returned string was visibly garbled and was excluded rather than repaired. Anyone mirroring these sources should re-verify quote strings against the source text before publication.
contradictions: STATOR STOICHIOMETRY, 4:2 vs 5:2. Sowa & Berry (2008), from cross-linking and chromatography: "The stoichiometry of stator complexes deduced from targeted disulphide cross-linking studies and chromatography appears to be A4B2" (IF-32). Deme et al. (2020), from cryo-EM: "3D reconstructions of these complexes yielded volumes that could only be interpreted as MotA5B2 assemblies" (IF-01), independently matched by Santiveri et al. ("CjMotAB forms a 5:2 complex, as do SoMotAB and VaPomAB") and Hu et al. ("conserved 5:2 subunit stoichiometry"). Both recorded; not reconciled. The 4:2 figure is retained as a falsified claim because every downstream ions-per-revolution calculation depends on which number is used.

IONS PER STATOR UNIT PER REVOLUTION, ~10 vs 68 - a factor of about seven. Mora et al. (2009): "proton flux and motor rotation are always strongly coupled with ~10 protons passing through the membrane per MotA/B unit per rotation" (IF-11). Rieu et al. (2022): "Ten ions per revolution of the MotA pentamer then correspond to 10 x 34/5 = 68 ions per MotAB stator unit per revolution of the flagellar motor" (IF-10). Note both begin from 'ten ions per revolution' but of DIFFERENT objects - Mora's per motor rotation, Rieu's per MotA pentamer rotation, geared 34/5. Recorded side by side without choosing.

PROTONS PER MOTOR REVOLUTION, ~1200 vs everything else. Sowa & Berry (2008): "The estimated flux was around 1200 H+ ions per revolution per motor over a speed range of ~20-60 Hz" (IF-12). This cannot be squared with IF-11 (~10 per stator x ~11 stators, about 110) and sits well above IF-10 (68 x ~11, about 750). The 1200 figure is from Streptococcus (Meister et al. 1987) while the stator counts are from E. coli/Salmonella, so the mismatch may be species as much as method. The review itself hedges it as uncertain "due mainly to the difficulty of counting flagellar filaments".

IS THE PLUG THE GATE? Homma & Kojima (2022): the plug "is proposed to regulate the ion-conducting activity of the stator, by 'plugging' the channel" (IF-17); Nakamura & Minamino (2019): it "binds to the H+ channel to suppress massive H+ flow" (IF-20). Against this, Deme et al. (2020): "our structures show that the plug helices are not the sole block to ion permeation since there are no detectable channels across the cytoplasmic membrane compartment" (IF-19). Both sides recorded. The deletion phenotype - massive proton influx (IF-18) - is agreed by all sources; what is contested is whether the plug ALONE closes the channel.

DOES REMOVING THE PLUG OPEN THE PERIPLASMIC ENTRY? Santiveri et al. (C. jejuni MotAB): an access pathway to MotB D22 from the periplasm exists in the unplugged structure but not the plugged one (IF-05). Nishikino et al. (marine Vibrio PomAB, 2025): the periplasmic side of the tunnel remains closed even with plug removal, implying further structural change is needed for ion uptake (IF-26). Different species, different coupling ion, opposite conclusions about the same step. Not reconciled.

IS MOTOR SPEED LINEAR IN PMF? Biquet-Bisquert et al. (2021) report the consensus - "numerous results contribute to a general consensus that there exists a linear relationship between the speed of the motor and IMF" - and, in the same section, the counter-observation: "a decrease of pH_ext from 7 to 5 leads to a total decrease in PMF of only ~ 10 mV, yet causes a strong decline in motor speed" (IF-35). This matters beyond the motor: two of the PMF measurements recorded here (IF-30, IF-36) USE motor speed as their PMF instrument and therefore assume the linearity that the second sentence strains.

MEMBRANE POTENTIAL / PMF MAGNITUDE - four different numbers, recorded as a spread and NOT averaged. Measured: delta p about -165 mV (Kashket 1985, IF-29) and membrane potential about -160 mV (Krasnopeeva et al. 2019, IF-30). Quoted as typical: "around -150 mV" (Sowa & Berry 2008, IF-31). Assumed in a model, and quoted without a sign: "membrane potential 120 mV" (Bai et al. 2009, IF-37). Separately, Terradot et al. (preprint) use delta-psi about -140 mV with a delta-pH of 1.5 contributing -90 mV (IF-36), a decomposition that does not obviously sum to the others.

APPARENT CONTRADICTION THAT IS NOT ONE - the conserved aspartate carries four different numbers. Asp32 (E. coli MotB, IF-03), Asp33 (Salmonella MotB, IF-04), D22 (Campylobacter jejuni MotB, IF-05/IF-07), D24 (Vibrio PomB, IF-22/IF-25). Nakamura & Minamino state the correspondence explicitly for the first two: "Asp-33 of Salmonella MotB, which corresponds to Asp-32 in E. coli MotB". Flagged because a careless merge would read as four different residues rather than one residue under four numbering schemes - AND because no source fetched this session stated the C. jejuni or Vibrio correspondences explicitly, so those two alignments are NOT verified here.

STEP SIZE FOR THE SAME 26 STEPS PER REVOLUTION. Sowa & Berry (2008): "The most probable step size of 13.7 degrees corresponds to 26 steps per revolution (360/13.7=26.3)". Mora et al. (2009): "The steps have average size ~1.7 degrees, which corresponds to 26 steps per rotation". 1.7 degrees does not give 26 steps per rotation; 13.7 does. One of these is very likely a transcription or typographical artefact - possibly introduced by the fetch layer rather than present in the source - but I did not verify raw source bytes, so both are recorded as fetched and neither is silently corrected.

SELECTIVITY FILTER LOCATION IN THE SAME PROTEIN. Hu et al. (2023) place Na+/K+/H+ discrimination in a selectivity cavity of three conserved threonines (T158, T185, T186), stating "H+ is too small to fill this cavity" (IF-23). Nishikino et al. (2025) place the size filter in Cavity-I on the PERIPLASMIC side, an approximately 6 A hydrophobic cavity, with the threonines instead making the CYTOPLASMIC Cavity-II hydrophilic (IF-26). Both are Vibrio PomAB, both cryo-EM, both propose a size-based filter - and they put it in different places. Recorded as agreement on mechanism-type and disagreement on location.
couldNotVerify: THE PLUG'S PRIMARY GENETICS. Hosking, Vogt, Bakker & Manson (2006), J Mol Biol 364, 921-937, 'The Escherichia coli MotAB proton channel unplugged' - the paper that defines the plug. ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403 and no PMC copy was found. The claims that the plug is an amphipathic alpha helix flanked by Pro52 and Pro65, that deleting MotB residues 51-70 causes massive proton influx WITHOUT significantly depleting the proton motive force, and that Ile58/Tyr61/Phe62 are essential for plug function, appeared ONLY in a WebSearch summary. They are NOT recorded as signals. The 'without significantly depleting the PMF' clause is the most interesting of them and remains unverified.

THE PROTONS-PER-REVOLUTION NUMBER IN ITS PRIMARY. Meister, Lowe & Berg (1987), Cell 49, 643-650. cell.com returned HTTP 403; only the Europe PMC abstract was read, and it contains NO numeric flux value. The ~1200 H+ per revolution figure is recorded (IF-12) solely as Sowa & Berry's restatement. The method, the filament-counting correction and the error bars are unread.

SPEED PROPORTIONAL TO PMF AT LIGHT LOAD. Gabel & Berg (2003), PNAS 100, 8748-8751. pnas.org returned HTTP 403. Never read. No row is recorded for the foundational speed-versus-PMF linearity result; IF-35 records only a review's restatement of the consensus AND its counter-example.

THE PUBLISHED VERSION OF THE SANTIVERI STRUCTURES. Santiveri et al. (2020), Cell 183(1), 244-257. cell.com returned HTTP 403. Every D22, F186 and access-pathway quote in IF-05, IF-06, IF-07 and IF-18 comes from the bioRxiv PREPRINT (2020.05.15.096610v1); the peer-reviewed wording may differ.

NONEQUIVALENCE OF MEMBRANE VOLTAGE AND ION GRADIENT. Lo, Leake, Pilizota & Berry (2007), Biophys J 93, 294-302 - the result that the two components of the driving force are NOT interchangeable at low load. Located in search but NEVER FETCHED. A significant gap: it bears directly on whether PMF can be treated as a single scalar in any B0 model.
POWERING THE MOTOR WITH AN EXTERNAL VOLTAGE SOURCE. Fung & Berg (1995), Nature 375, 809-812. Never fetched; referenced only inside the Biquet-Bisquert review.

SINGLE-STATOR ION FLUX IN E. COLI. No source read this session reports a DIRECT measurement of proton flux through a single E. coli stator unit. Every per-stator number recorded (IF-10, IF-11, IF-37) is derived or assumed. The only direct flux measurement found is Meister 1987, in Streptococcus, abstract-only. This is the specific hole the B0 layer has.

(2017) as ref 29 — the catch-bond attribution chain is visible in the fetched source, not assumed.

TRIANGULATION ACHIEVED: load→recruitment independently reported by the Berg lab (Lele 2013) and the Berry/Armitage lab (Tipping 2013). The catch-bond reading independently reported by the Pedaci/Berry lab (Nord 2017) and the Berg/Tu lab (Wadhwa 2019, 2021). Force-from-lipids independently reported by Reddy et al. (2019) and Park et al. (2023) for MscS and Bavi et al. (2016) for MscL.

TRIANGULATION NOT ACHIEVED: the Ito et al. (2021) rotation-not-load claim has no second source here. Neither does the Deme et al. structural material (preprint only; I did not read the published Nature Microbiology version).
contradictions: SHARPEST CONTRADICTION — ROTATION vs TORQUE, same year, same symmetry experiment, opposite conclusions. Wadhwa, Tu & Berg (2021, PNAS 118(15), e2024608118): "the remodeling dynamics as a function of motor torque are identical in CW and CCW rotating motors" and "torque is the main parameter governing load-dependent stator remodeling", adding "No collapse was seen when the data were plotted against the motor rotation speed". Ito, Nakamura & Toyabe (2021, Nat Commun 12, 3218): "This supports that the binding is regulated not by the load on the previously bound stator units even at small N but by the rotation rate", reasoning that "The binding is enhanced in either rotational direction despite that the load on the stator is different between them". Both groups used direction symmetry; one concluded torque, the other rotation. Organism differs (E. coli vs Salmonella) but NEITHER source proposes that as the reconciliation, so I do not assert it.

STALL — MOST STATORS or FEWEST? Tipping et al. (2013, mBio 4(4), e00551-13): "our experiments with stalled motors (Fig. 4) showed that motor rotation is not required for stator binding" and "Indeed, motor stall, which corresponds to the largest torque in our experiments, induced the largest number of bound stators that we observed." Ito et al. (2021): "The stator binding is slow at the stalled state, but the rotation in either direction boosts the stator binding." Opposite claims about the same experimental condition. Nord et al. (2017) sits in between: they measure recruitment DURING stall (up to 2.3±1.8 units) at low prior load, supporting Tipping, but no change (−0.3±1.1) at the highest load.

STATOR OCCUPANCY AT ZERO LOAD — 1-2 UNITS or ZERO? Lele, Hosu & Berg (2013, PNAS 110(29)): "one or sometimes two stator elements drive a motor near zero load". Wadhwa, Phillips & Berg (2019, PNAS 116(24)): "The number of stator units bound to the motor varied from ≈10 near stall to 0 at zero load." Both E. coli, both from the Berg laboratory, six years apart. The 2019 paper frames itself as having "closed this gap" relative to earlier work where stoichiometry "changed by at most 2-3 units", presenting its range as an extension rather than a correction — but the zero-load endpoint numerically disagrees with the 2013 paper.

DOES SPEED AFFECT THE ON RATE? Wadhwa, Phillips & Berg (2019): "A model in which speed affects the binding rate and torque affects the free energy of bound stator units captures the observed torque-dependent stator assembly dynamics" — speed has a distinct role in association. Wadhwa, Tu & Berg (2021), Fig. 4 caption: "The dashed line is k+ = 0.0016 s−1", i.e. the ON rate is fitted as torque-INDEPENDENT and constant, all mechanosensitivity being placed in the OFF rate k−=k+e(ΔF0−λΓ)/kBT. Same senior author, two years apart. Summarising either paper as "the motor senses torque" discards the 2019 speed term.

WHERE IS THE FORCE-GATED BOND — CELL-WALL SIDE or ROTOR SIDE? Nord et al. (2017) locate it at the anchor: "The interface between the PG and the MotB PG-binding (PGB) domain, located at the C-terminal of MotB (MotBC), is where the force can have an impact on the bonds relevant for the lifetime of the stator unit around the rotor." Chawla, Ford & Lele (2017, Sci Rep 7, 5565) locate the gating at the rotor: "the torque generated by individual stator-units modulates the accessibility of cryptic binding sites, thereby controlling the binding-affinity to the rotor." Bond-lifetime gating at the cell wall versus affinity gating at the rotor are different mechanisms; both are hypotheses and both papers hedge.

THE CATCH BOND IS KINETICALLY INFERRED AND STRUCTURALLY UNOBSERVED — a tension across sources rather than between them. Nord et al. (2017) state plainly: "While our data indicate a catch-bond mechanism, they cannot discriminate any structural detail." Deme et al. (2020 preprint) could not resolve the very domain proposed to carry the load: "Although we do not observe the PGB-domains of MotB in the resolved structures" and "the PGB-domain of MotB has no fixed location with respect to the core complex in the context of the isolated protein." No source I read this session provides a structural observation of the proposed force-bearing interface.

MotA4B2 SUPERSEDED BY MotA5B2. Deme et al. (2020 preprint) note that pre-structural mechanistic hypotheses "explicitly use the predicted 2-fold symmetry of a MotA4B2 complex", then report "3D reconstructions of these complexes yielded volumes that could only be interpreted as MotA5B2 assemblies". Any mechanosensing model in the pre-2020 literature built on 4-fold stator symmetry rests on a stoichiometry this structural work contradicts.

MEASURED ON-RATES DIFFER BY ~3 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE ACROSS THE TWO CAMPS, though not as like-for-like quantities. Wadhwa, Tu & Berg (2021) fit k+ = 0.0016 s−1. Ito et al. (2021) report "The average of b in the CCW rotation was 1.3 ± 0.1 s−1" and separately "k = k+ + k− = 0.080 s−1". Different models, different organisms, different definitions; I did NOT establish a conversion and record the discrepancy rather than reconcile it.

contradictions: COOPERATIVITY IS NOT IN THE BINDING STEP. Sourjik & Berg (2002, PMC130518) measured CheY~P/FliM binding in vivo by FRET and got a Hill coefficient of 1.7 ± 0.3 (and 1.8 ± 0.3 in a companion fit), while the motor's switching response fitted to Cluzel et al.'s data gives 10.3 — IN THE SAME SECTION OF THE SAME PAPER. Their words: "Binding of CheY∼P to FliM was found to be much less cooperative than motor switching." This is not an error to reconcile; it is the central structural constraint of the domain — whatever generates the ultrasensitivity happens AFTER binding, which is precisely what conformational-spread models (SC-31, SC-34) exist to explain.

THREE DIFFERENT DISSOCIATION CONSTANTS ARE IN CIRCULATION FOR WHAT SOUNDS LIKE ONE INTERACTION, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS. (a) 3.7 ± 0.4 μM — Sourjik & Berg 2002, in vivo FRET, CheY~P binding to FliM. (b) 3.1 μM — used by Yuan et al. 2012 ("K=3.1 μM") and Antani et al. 2021 ("a dissociation constant value (KD) = 3.1 μM based on previous studies"), both attributing it to prior work, and both applying it to the MOTOR-BIAS relation rather than to binding. (c) ~450 μM — Wheatley et al. 2020, in vitro, NONPHOSPHORYLATED CheY binding the FliM N-terminal peptide, stated to be 15× weaker than CheY~P. These must NOT be averaged or treated as replicates of one measurement. Recorded side by side, unreconciled.

WHAT DRIVES FliM REMODELLING — TWO 2012 PAPERS FROM THE SAME LABORATORY DISAGREE. Yuan, Branch, Hosu & Berg (Nature 2012): "The number of FliM subunits in the C-ring increases in response to a decrement in the concentration of CheY-P, increasing motor sensitivity." Lele, Branch, Nathan & Berg (PNAS 2012): "We show here that the number of FliM molecules in the motor and the fraction of FliM molecules that exchange depend on the direction of flagellar rotation, not on CheY-P binding per se." The first makes CheY-P concentration the causal variable; the second explicitly denies that CheY-P binding is the causal variable and substitutes rotation direction. Both fetched and quoted verbatim. Not reconciled.

THE CCW FliM COUNT DIFFERS BETWEEN SOURCES. Lele et al. 2012: "there are ∼44 molecules in a motor that rotates exclusively counterclockwise" — note their own preface, "Assuming that there are ∼34 molecules of FliM in a motor that rotates exclusively clockwise", i.e. the CW figure is an assumed anchor. Hosu & Berg 2018: motors rotating exclusively CCW have "∼45 copies of each" (FliM and FliN). A small discrepancy, but recorded because both are hedged approximations resting on an assumed CW baseline rather than on independent absolute counts.

THE POLARITY OF METHYLATION IS STATED IN OPPOSITE TERMS BY TWO REVIEWS. Parkinson, Hazelbauer & Falke (2015): CheR "catalyzes a glutamyl methylation reaction that shifts output toward the ON state." Salah Ud-Din & Roujeinikova (2017): "Elevated methylation results in inhibition of MCP signaling." These are plausibly using "signalling"/"output" to denote different quantities (kinase activation vs. ligand-responsiveness), but NEITHER fetched page stated which, so the apparent contradiction stands as read and is not resolved here.

WHERE CheY-P ACTS: FliM OR FliN. Sourjik & Berg (2002) treat FliM as THE target and measure CheY~P/FliM occupancy directly. Sarkar, Paul & Blair (2010) title their paper "CheY binds to the rotor protein FliN to control the direction of flagellar rotation" and propose that "the N-terminal segment of FliM serves to capture CheYP, and that switching is triggered by the subsequent interaction of this FliM-bound CheYP with FliN." The two-stage proposal (echoed by Wheatley et al. 2020) is a candidate resolution, but note it is offered by its authors as a PROPOSAL ("We propose that..."), and Sarkar et al.'s page carried NO measured dissociation constant supporting the FliN step. Recorded as an open disagreement about the locus of the trigger, not as a settled hand-off.

THE SWITCH IS DESCRIBED BOTH PROBABILISTICALLY AND DETERMINISTICALLY BY OVERLAPPING AUTHOR GROUPS. Hazelbauer, Falke & Parkinson (TIBS): phospho-CheY binds the motor "enhancing the probability of clockwise (CW) rotation". Parkinson, Hazelbauer & Falke (2015): "Phospho-CheY interacts with the flagellar basal body to trigger CW rotation." The 2015 wording drops the probabilistic qualifier. Minor, but it matters for anyone building a model: the earlier phrasing is the one consistent with the stochastic switching that conformational-spread models reproduce.

h=10 IS USED AS A GLOBAL CONSTANT BY SOURCES THAT CITE A SOURCE QUALIFYING IT AS LOCAL. Ma et al. (2012) state the coefficient "is ∼10 at the most sensitive part of the region of operation" — a local slope. Antani et al. (2021) write "We assumed ... a Hill coefficient value (h) = 10" and apply it as a fixed parameter across their fitted curves. This is not a contradiction between measurements but a contradiction between a qualified claim and its unqualified reuse, and it is the kind that propagates silently.

contradictions: AQP2 PHOSPHORYLATION — TRAFFICKING ONLY, OR ALSO INTRINSIC CHANNEL ACTIVITY? Ando & Uchida (2018, PMC5956045, Introduction) state 'Changes in AQP2 phosphorylation status promote AQP2 trafficking to the apical plasma membrane, which results in water reabsorption from urine', and Wilson, Miranda & Knepper (2013, PMC3775849, Section B.1) attribute the permeability rise to 'recruitment of AQP2 to the apical plasma membrane'. Eto et al. (2010, PMC3003378, Abstract) report the opposite emphasis from a cell-free system: 'PKA phosphorylation significantly increased the osmotic water permeability of AQP2-reconstituted liposomes', with their Introduction naming the open question directly — 'whether this phosphorylation regulates the water permeability of individual AQP2 proteins still remains unclear.' BOTH RECORDED. These may be complementary rather than exclusive, but a model that represents the vasopressin gate as PURELY a trafficking gate is contradicted by fetched evidence and must not be stated as settled.

WITHIN Wilson, Miranda & Knepper (2013, PMC3775849, Section A.1) — SER256 OCCUPANCY MOVES THE WRONG WAY. The same page that names Ser256 as the PKA substrate triggering membrane accumulation reports the quantification as 'Ser256 phosphorylation: control, 49% of total; vasopressin, 34% of total' — a FALL on vasopressin exposure — while Ser269 rises from 3% to 26%. This is an internal tension in the fetched source between the mechanistic narrative and the tabulated stoichiometry. I did not reconcile it and did not fetch the underlying primary quantifications.

SOMATOSTATIN RECEPTOR SUBTYPE ON THE BETA CELL. Schwetz, Ustione & Piston (2013, PMC3543566, Introduction) state 'SST receptors (SSTRs) are highly expressed in the β-cell, with SSTR1 and -5 being the predominant receptor subtypes'. Hart et al. (2025 preprint, PMC12642553, Results) state the segregation differently: 'SSTR2 on exclusively α cells', with SSTR3 the beta-cell receptor on primary cilia. These name DIFFERENT RECEPTORS on the same cell type. The sources differ in date (2013 vs 2025), in method, and in peer-review status (peer-reviewed vs preprint) — but both are recorded as fetched rather than deferring to the newer or the older.

WHERE SOMATOSTATIN'S STOP ACTUALLY LANDS — BETA-CELL CALCIUM, OR THE ALPHA CELL? Schwetz et al. (2013) conclude 'SST attenuates secretion through Gβγ inhibition of Ca2+ activity', reporting 'SST decreased the [Ca2+]i oscillation frequency (P < 0.04)' — a DIRECT effect on beta-cell calcium. Hart et al. (2025 preprint) route the dominant effect INDIRECTLY through the alpha cell (SSTR2, suppress glucagon, remove glucagon's paracrine potentiation of insulin) and describe the direct beta-cell action as acting on cAMP while being 'less effective in inhibiting β cell Ca2+'. Direct-on-calcium versus indirect-via-paracrine-partner are materially different comparator topologies; both recorded.

PROTON EXCLUSION BY AQUAPORINS — ARE THE NPA MOTIFS SUFFICIENT? Wu et al. (2009, PMC2726698, Abstract/Results) state explicitly: 'Contrary to theoretical models, we found that electrostatic repulsion at the central asn-pro-ala (NPA) region does not suffice to exclude protons' and 'Full proton exclusion is reached only in conjunction with the aromatic/arginine (ar/R) constriction at the pore mouth.' The source itself names the prior theoretical models it contradicts. Hub & de Groot (2008, PMC2234115, Results) independently reach a compatible conclusion for uncharged solutes: 'the highly conserved NPA motifs are not involved in the selectivity for uncharged solutes'. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES — one experimental, one simulation — AGAINST THE NPA-CENTRED ACCOUNT. Recorded because the NPA-only story remains the common textbook framing, so a comparator model built from a textbook would encode the contradicted version.

CALCIUM'S SIGN AS AN AQUAPORIN GATING INPUT IS OPPOSITE IN TWO SYSTEMS. Ozu et al. (2022, PMC9604103, Section 3.2, PLANT PIPs) state that 'intracellular calcium DEPLETION' is among the 'conditions that favor the closed state of the channel'. Fields et al. (2017, PMC5217678) state for mammalian AQP0 that permeability falls in response to INCREASES in calcium, via calmodulin. Both quoted as printed. These are different proteins in different kingdoms and are not necessarily in conflict — but they cannot be merged into a single 'calcium gates aquaporins' rule, and any model that does so will carry the sign backwards for one of them.

'ADRENALINE STOPS INSULIN SECRETION' IS CONDITIONAL, NOT GENERAL. Sluga et al. (2022, PMC9640998) report that '0.5 nM' adrenaline — 'the lowest measured physiological concentration' — inhibited calcium events at 8 mM glucose, but that 'A glucose increase to 12 mM...was sufficient to override the inhibitory effect of adrenaline', requiring 'an order of magnitude higher adrenaline concentration'. Their abstract states glucose stimulates 'beyond levels that could be inhibited with physiologically available plasma adrenaline concentration.' This contradicts the unqualified textbook STOP and is an adverse result against any comparator model in which an inhibitory input can always veto an excitatory one.

AN INVERSION THAT READS AS A CONTRADICTION AND IS NOT — FLAGGED BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST LIKELY MODELLING ERROR IN THIS DOMAIN. In the beta cell, the SECRETING state corresponds to the KATP channel being CLOSED and the RESTING/OFF state to it being OPEN (Ashcroft 2023, PMC10202764: 'At low (substimulatory) blood glucose levels, the channel was open and the β-cell was electrically silent'; 'This closes the KATP channels, thereby producing a membrane depolarization'). In the water systems (aquaporin, VRAC), OPEN means flux and CLOSED means no flux. 'Open' therefore maps to 'go' in one half of this domain and to 'stop' in the other. Recorded as a contradiction in VOCABULARY, not in biology.

contradictions: FORMAL VALIDITY OF THE FEP DERIVATION. Biehl, Pollock & Kanai (S04) state verbatim: 'We prove by counterexample that the original free energy lemma, when taken at face value, is wrong', and that Markov blanket definitions across works 'are not equivalent'. Friston (S01/S02) presents that lemma and that blanket construct as the basis of the claim that internal states 'will appear to minimize a free energy functional'. Both sides fetched and read this session. NOT RECONCILED HERE. Biehl et al.'s own hedge is preserved: 'These problems do not rule out conclusively that the general ideas behind the free energy principle are worth pursuing.'

SCOPE OF THE FEP. Aguilera, Millidge, Tschantz & Buckley (S05) find the Markov blanket condition and the solenoidal-flow restrictions 'only valid for a very narrow space of parameters', and that a mathematically central step 'does not hold in general even for linear systems'. Sakthivadivel (S09) replies that 'their derivations are largely correct, but where their arguments are not fatal to the FEP', offering 'a path-based formulation of the FEP' that 'restore[s] its explanatory power in broad physical regimes'. Both fetched. NOTE: the critic's derivations are CONCEDED as correct — the live dispute is whether a reformulation rescues the principle, not whether the algebra held.

METAPHYSICAL STATUS OF MARKOV BLANKETS. Bruineberg, Dołęga, Dewhurst & Baltieri (S06) argue the metaphysical use of blankets 'cannot be justified by an appeal to the success of the mathematical framework alone', coining 'Pearl blankets' vs 'Friston blankets'. Ramstead (S08) replies critically to exactly that distinction. Both fetched — BUT only Bruineberg et al.'s substantive position was obtainable; Ramstead's fetched abstract announces a critique without stating its content. RECORDED AS OPEN AND UNRESOLVED IN THE EVIDENCE I HOLD.

DIRECTION OF DESCENT, FLAGELLUM vs TYPE III SECRETION SYSTEM. Miller (S18) argues irreducible complexity collapsed because 'a simpler, functional system (the TTSS) has been discovered among the protein components of the flagellum', framing the TTSS as the simpler pre-existing system. Abby & Rocha (S21) report that '84% of the trees support the flagellum-first hypothesis, arguing strongly against ... that flagella were derived from an NF-T3SS', concluding the injectisome 'arose via exaptation of the flagellum'. BOTH ARE FETCHED, BOTH ARE MAINSTREAM, AND BOTH REJECT DESIGN — yet they disagree on which came first, and the intelligent-design page (S16) cites the flagellum-first direction in its own favour. Carry this forward unsmoothed: Miller's 'a functional subset exists, therefore not irreducible' argument SURVIVES S21 (the subset still exists), but his implied precursor ordering does not.

RECONSTRUCTION OF FLAGELLAR CORE EVOLUTION. Liu & Ochman (S20) conclude core flagellar components 'originated through the successive duplication and modification of a few, or perhaps even a single, precursor gene'. Doolittle & Zhaxybayeva (S22) describe a recent scheme for flagellar evolution as '(perhaps too simple)'. PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED: the fetched Doolittle abstract does not name its target, and the full text was blocked (HTTP 403), so the identification of Liu & Ochman as the target — and the reported objections about e-value cutoffs and discordant gene trees — rest on search-result prose I did not confirm at source.

signals.whatCrosses: water fails to be reabsorbed and leaves the body as dilute urine

The consequence of losing the gate is 'increased excretion of diluted urine in spite of appropriate secretion of the antidiuretic hormone vasopressin' — the hormone is PRESENT and the transfer still does not happen, which is the signature of a broken gate rather than a missing signal. The source restates the normal cascade: 'Binding of vasopressin to its receptor V2R in the renal collecting ducts increases intracellular production of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), which then activates cAMP-dependent protein kinase, PKA'.

signals.organism: multiple mammalian cell types (HEK293 and glioblastoma cells cited)
signals.verbatimQuote: Piezo1 activity increases upon hypotonic-induced cell swelling in a variety of cells
signals.quoteLocator: Section: Piezo1 channel structure, gating, and biophysical properties
signals.mechanismStated: A mechanically-gated non-selective cation channel acts as the SENSOR of the boundary's own deformation and converts it into a chemical signal: 'Piezo channels display all the features of mechanosensitivity and respond to a variety of mechanical stimuli, including membrane stretch and cell swelling', and 'Piezo1 channels are permeable to monovalent (K+, Na+, and Cs+) and divalent (Ba2+, Ca2+, and Mg2+) cations, with a selectivity sequence of Ca2+ > K+ > Na+ > Mg2+'. The Ca2+ then opens downstream effluxes: 'Piezo1-mediated Ca2+ influx has been shown to regulate cell volume by activating the KCa channels IK and BK', and 'In HEK293 cells, the mechanism by which Piezo1 modulates cell volume involves the modulation of VRAC-mediated ICl,swell, through the CICR mechanism'.
signals.quantityIfStated: 'The unitary conductance recorded in cell-attached configuration is ~ 35 pS'; 'inactivation time of approximately 15 ms at − 80 mV'; 'During cell swelling, global cytosolic Ca2+ levels have been reported to raise up to 400 nM'; IK channels 'EC50: 100–200 nM' for Ca2+; BK channels 'EC50: 1–5 µM'

signals.layer: volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC/LRRC8) in the plasma membrane
signals.whatCrosses: Cl− and small organic compounds (osmolytes) out; water follows osmotically
signals.signalName: VRAC/LRRC8 is opened by cell swelling and releases osmolytes to drive regulatory volume decrease
signals.organism: mammalian cells (LRRC8A–E family); macrophage example cited
signals.verbatimQuote: the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) is a particular type of anion channel. VRAC is activated by cell swelling and mediates the transport of Cl− and small organic compounds
signals.mechanismStated: The channel is gated by the very quantity it regulates — swelling opens it, and its flux reverses the swelling: 'The VRAC-mediated transport of ions and osmolytes leads to water efflux and thereby returns the cell volume back to normal, a process that is called regulatory volume decrease (RVD)'. This is negative feedback closing through the physical medium (osmotic water movement) rather than through a signalling pathway. The source also notes cargo beyond osmolytes: 'VRAC containing LRRC8C and/or LRRC8E isoforms in macrophages transports an immunotransmitter, 2′3′cyclic-GMP-AMP (cGAMP)'.
signals.quantityIfStated: NOT STATED on fetched page — the extraction explicitly reported that no conductance (pS), ionic strength (mM) or osmolarity (mOsm) values appear anywhere on this structural-biology review page.

signals.layer: autocrine extracellular signalling loop that amplifies the volume-regulatory response
signals.whatCrosses: ATP out of the swollen cell into the extracellular space; then Ca2+ mobilised internally; then K+ and Cl− out
signals.signalName: Swelling releases ATP which acts back on P2Y2 receptors to augment regulatory volume decrease
signals.organism: multiple cell types (epithelial and other cultured lines discussed)
signals.verbatimQuote: swelling-induced ATP release facilitates RVD by augmenting cytosolic Ca2+ mobilization via G protein-coupled, PLC-linked P2Y2 receptors.
signals.quoteLocator: Section: ATP receptor-mediated upregulation of volume-regulatory K+, but not Cl−, channels
signals.mechanismStated: The cell reports its own swelling to itself through the OUTSIDE: 'Osmotic cell swelling has been found to induce the release of ATP from many cell types', the released ATP reaches a receptor-activating concentration at the cell surface, and 'Swelling-induced ATP release has recently been shown to augment the Ca2+ response to a hypotonic challenge via stimulation of P2Y2 receptors.' The effluxes that restore volume are named: 'a volume-regulatory KCl efflux is induced as a result of the activation of K+ and Cl− channels in most cell types or as a result of electroneutral operation of cotransporters, such as the K+−Cl− symporter', and of the anion channels 'the most ubiquitous and specific is the volume-sensitive outwardly rectifying (VSOR) anion channel.' The section title records a SELECTIVE effect: the ATP loop upregulates the K+ channels but NOT the Cl− channels.
signals.quantityIfStated: 'By a biosensor technique, the extracellular ATP concentration in the immediate vicinity of the cell surface was observed to reach over 10 μm, which is high enough to stimulate purinergic receptors.' Also on the page: apoptotic volume decrease 'within 2 h' and shrinkage 'as early as 30 min after stimulation with TNFα'.
signals.apaReference: Okada, Y., Maeno, E., Shimizu, T., Dezaki, K., Wang, J., & Morishima, S. (2001). Receptor-mediated control of regulatory volume decrease (RVD) and apoptotic volume decrease (AVD). The Journal of Physiology, 532(1), 3–16. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-7793.2001.0003g.x
signals.openAccess: Page states only '© The Physiological Society 2001'. No Creative Commons licence stated.
signals.confidenceNote: The '10 μm' in the quote is as printed on the page; in context this is micromolar with the case lost in rendering, and I flag that rather than silently correcting the source. This review is from 2001 and PREDATES the 2014 identification of LRRC8 as the VRAC/VSOR pore — it names the current but could not name the protein; read alongside CMP-17 for the molecular identity. The K+-selective / Cl−-non-selective asymmetry of the ATP loop is exactly the kind of detail a model would flatten if it treated 'RVD' as one switch.

signals.layer: pancreatic beta cell plasma membrane — metabolic state gating hormone release
signals.whatCrosses: K+ stops crossing as the channel closes; then Ca2+ crosses IN through voltage-gated channels; then insulin crosses OUT by exocytosis
signals.signalName: Glucose to ATP/ADP ratio to KATP closure to depolarisation to Ca2+ influx to insulin secretion
signals.organism: pancreatic beta cell (mouse and human islets discussed)
signals.verbatimQuote: This closes the KATP channels, thereby producing a membrane depolarization that opens voltage-gated calcium channels and triggers electrical activity, calcium influx, and insulin secretion.
signals.quoteLocator: Section: Metabolic Regulation of the KATP Channel
signals.mechanismStated: The immediately preceding sentence states the input: 'when blood glucose levels rise, glucose metabolism increases the relative amount of ATP and decreases that of MgADP (abbreviated here as an increase in the ATP-to-ADP ratio).' The comparator is metabolic: the channel reads a RATIO, not an absolute concentration, and converts it to membrane voltage, which is converted to Ca2+ concentration, which is converted to secretion — four different physical currencies in series, each gating the next.
signals.quantityIfStated: NOT STATED for this specific mechanistic sentence; the page's quantitative statements concern disease context ('culture of human islets at just 8 mmol/L glucose decreases both stimulated insulin secretion and insulin content'; variant mice 'secreted less insulin at a threshold level of 7 mmol/L glucose').

signals.layer: pancreatic beta cell plasma membrane — the resting/OFF state
signals.whatCrosses: K+ out of the cell, holding the membrane hyperpolarised; Ca2+ and insulin do NOT cross
signals.signalName: Low glucose and MgADP hold KATP open — K+ efflux switches insulin release off
signals.verbatimQuote: The resulting potassium efflux holds the β-cell membrane hyperpolarized and switches off electrical activity, calcium influx, and insulin release.
signals.quoteLocator: Section: Metabolic Regulation of the KATP Channel
signals.mechanismStated: The STOP is not an added inhibitor but the DEFAULT state of the channel: 'At low (substimulatory) blood glucose levels, the channel was open and the β-cell was electrically silent', and 'channel activity is increased by MgADP.' MgADP is an ACTIVE opener, so falling glucose does not merely remove a closing signal — it supplies an opening one. The resting condition of this gate is actively maintained, which matters for any model that treats 'off' as the absence of input.
signals.quantityIfStated: NOT STATED alongside this sentence on the fetched page — no MgADP concentration, membrane potential value or K+ current magnitude accompanies it.
signals.apaReference: Ashcroft, F. M. (2023). KATP channels and the metabolic regulation of insulin secretion in health and disease: The 2022 Banting Medal for Scientific Achievement Award Lecture. Diabetes, 72(6), 693–702. https://doi.org/10.2337/dbi22-0030

signals.confidenceNote: Directly answers the operator's 'what stops it' for insulin: falling glucose is a stop signal implemented by an ion channel that OPENS. Note the inversion that trips people up — the STOP state is the channel OPEN state and the GO state is the channel CLOSED state. Any comparator diagram that maps 'open' to 'go' will get this system backwards.

signals.layer: beta cell triggering pathway resolved into named stages with parameters, plus a second KATP-independent amplifying layer
signals.whatCrosses: glucose in via transporters, K+ blocked, Ca2+ in via VDCC, insulin out
signals.signalName: Triggering pathway is necessary but not sufficient — KATP-independent amplifying pathways set Ca2+ sensitivity
signals.organism: human and mouse beta cells (explicitly compared)
signals.verbatimQuote: This triggering pathway is essential, i.e. necessary, but not very efficient without so-called amplifying pathways which mainly affect the sensitivity of the secretory machinery to [Ca2+]C.
signals.mechanismStated: The full stated sequence: 'It consists of several events starting with influx of glucose through glucose transporters, glucose metabolism increasing intracellular ATP concentration, and triggering closure of ATP-dependent K+ channels (KATP channels). The resulting decrease in K+ efflux causes membrane depolarization, the consequent opening of voltage dependent calcium (Ca2+) channels (VDCC), and influx of Ca2+ ions.' On top of it sit at least two further pathways: 'there seem to be a KATP-independent Ca2+-dependent and a KATP-independent Ca2+-independent amplifying pathway.' The gate therefore has a trigger AND a gain control, and the gain control does not run through the trigger's channel at all.

signals.organism: mouse pancreatic islet (alpha and beta cells)
signals.verbatimQuote: Somatostatin signals through a family of 5 different inhibitory G protein coupled (Gαi GPCR) SST receptors
signals.mechanismStated: The transduction step is stated plainly — 'The Gαi subunit inhibits adenylyl cyclase and reduces the production of the secondary messenger cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)' — and the topology is the contribution: receptors segregate by cell type, with 'SSTR2 on exclusively α cells' and 'SSTR3 is expressed on primary cilia of islet cells' (beta cells SSTR3, alpha cells SSTR2). signals.whatCrosses: adrenaline onto alpha-2 adrenergic receptors; downstream, reduced cAMP and a desensitised exocytotic machinery
signals.signalName: Adrenaline stops insulin secretion via alpha-2 adrenergic Gi — but fails above a glucose threshold
signals.organism: mouse pancreatic islets (fresh tissue, calcium imaging)
signals.verbatimQuote: The stimulation of α2-adrenergic receptors on the plasma membrane of beta cells reduces their excitability and insulin secretion mostly through diminished cAMP production and downstream desensitization of late step(s) of exocytotic machinery to cytosolic Ca2+ concentration.
signals.mechanismStated: Transduction is stated as 'α2-receptors mediate the cellular signaling through the Gi-dependent mechanism, leading to inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (AC) activity.' Note WHERE the stop lands: not only on calcium, but on the SENSITIVITY of the exocytotic machinery to calcium — a gain change at the final step, downstream of the ion signal. The measured result is that this STOP is conditional on the strength of the GO: 'In some islets stimulated with 8 mM glucose, even the lowest measured physiological concentration of adrenaline (0.5 nM)...was able to inhibit [Ca2+]c events', but 'A glucose increase to 12 mM...was sufficient to override the inhibitory effect of adrenaline on beta cells...an order of magnitude higher adrenaline concentration in comparison to that used to inhibit 8 mM glucose.'

Frontiers in Endocrinology, 13, 1013697. https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2022.1013697

signals.confidenceNote: ADVERSE RESULT, STATED FIRST AND NOT SOFTENED: the paper's own abstract conclusion is that 'higher glucose concentrations stimulate beta cell activity in a non-linear manner and beyond levels that could be inhibited with physiologically available plasma adrenaline concentration.' The textbook line 'adrenaline stops insulin secretion' is therefore CONDITIONAL — it holds at moderate glucose and fails at high glucose within the physiological adrenaline range. For a comparator model this is the important row: the STOP has finite authority that the GO can exceed, so the two inputs do not compose as a simple switch. Mouse tissue; the human threshold is not established by this paper.

signals.organism: 41 flagellated bacterial species from 11 bacterial phyla
signals.verbatimQuote: These results show that core components of the bacterial flagellum originated through the successive duplication and modification of a few, or perhaps even a single, precursor gene.
signals.mechanismStated: From the abstract: the authors 'identified all homologs of all flagellar proteins encoded in the complete genome sequences of 41 flagellated species from 11 bacterial phyla' and 'could distinguish an ancient core set of 24 structural genes that were present in the common ancestor to all Bacteria', noting that 'many of these core genes show sequence similarity only to other flagellar core genes, indicating that they were derived from one another'.

signals.signalName: Flagellum-first: the non-flagellar T3SS arose by exaptation of the flagellum
signals.organism: >1,000 bacterial genomes; 155 genomes carrying NF-T3SSs and 642 carrying flagella
signals.verbatimQuote: 84% of the trees support the flagellum-first hypothesis, arguing strongly against an early split between flagella and NF-T3SSs or that flagella were derived from an NF-T3SS.
signals.mechanismStated: Verbatim: 'The phylogeny shows that the NF-T3SS arose via exaptation of the flagellum, i.e. the recruitment of part of the flagellum structure for the evolution of the new protein delivery function.' Author Summary, verbatim: 'We show that NF-T3SSs evolved from the flagellum by a series of genetic deletions, innovations, and recruitments of components from other cellular structures.'
signals.quantityIfStated: 'Our analysis of >1,000 genomes identified 921 T3SSs, including 222 NF-T3SSs'; '921 T3SSs: 222 NF-T3SSs and 699 flagella distributed among 155 and 642 genomes, respectively'; '84% of the trees'
signals.apaReference: Abby, S. S., & Rocha, E. P. C. (2012). The non-flagellar type III secretion system evolved from the bacterial flagellum and diversified into host-cell adapted systems. PLoS Genetics, 8(9), e1002983. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1002983
signals.openAccess: stated on page verbatim: '© Abby, Rocha. This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited.'
signals.confidenceNote: THIS ROW CUTS BOTH WAYS AND MUST NOT BE FLATTENED. It contradicts Miller's 2004 framing of the TTSS as the simpler system that came first (S18), and it agrees with a directional claim also made by the intelligent-design page (S16). It does NOT support a design inference: the paper's own framing is exaptation — the injectisome evolved FROM the flagellum 'by a series of genetic deletions, innovations, and recruitments'. The 84% figure is tree support, not a probability that the hypothesis is true.
